audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagreed with their own whys[] line — the sides read Skill / Camille / Camille / Skill / Skill / Camille / Camille while the prose says level 1 favours you, 2 and 3 even out, level 4 reclaims the lead, 6 is hers, and first item and late are yours.
audit.why: The packet levelChart is Wukong / Skill / Skill / Wukong / Camille / Wukong / Wukong, which matches the prose exactly and matches a 57.78% lane. Wukong's only losing stage is 6, where The Hextech Ultimatum anchors him for her full rotation.
audit.corrected: All seven rows rewritten in BOTH layers as matched pairs to Wukong / Skill / Skill / Wukong / Camille / Wukong / Wukong.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the ultimate was named "Hextech Ultimatum" — the packet flagged it and it is a real error.
audit.why: The ability is The Hextech Ultimatum, 140/115/90s. Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s and Precision Protocol is 9/8/7/6/5s. Against Warrior Trickster's 22s (per the mirror audit) those are the numbers the whole 'bait her E' plan runs on, and none of them were on the page.
audit.corrected: Full R name plus 140s written into spikes[1].text and phases[4].why; 16s Hookshot into phases[2].why, phases[5].why, spikes[2].text and the cooldown block; 9s Precision Protocol into phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text credited Wukong with a "Q true-damage armor shred", and Adaptive Defenses was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: The true damage in this matchup belongs to Camille's Precision Protocol, not to Crushing Blow — Crushing Blow cuts armour, which is exactly the stat her true damage ignores. And Adaptive Defenses shields her against the damage type that just hit her every time she autos a champion, which is why chip trading feeds her and burst does not. Hookshot also pulls her to a WALL, so terrain choice decides whether she has an engage at all.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text corrected to put the true damage on her Q; Adaptive Defenses named in the cooldown block; the wall requirement stated in phases[2].why and dontsFull[1].d.

notes: The packet's suspectName was a genuine error: the ability is The Hextech Ultimatum, not Hextech Ultimatum. The worse defect was attributing Camille's true damage to Wukong's Q — the page told the reader their armour shred was true damage, which inverts the one stat interaction that matters here. report[5].t and report[11].t still carry the old framing and would benefit from a sweep.
